Definition: prepared, i.e. full grown; spoken only (in plural) of he-goats, or (figuratively) leaders of the people
BiblicalUsage: The he-goat is the leader of the flock, and the word follows it from Jacob's flocks to the judgment of the shepherds. Jacob saw the rams leaping on the cattle in his dream, Moses says Israel ate the fat of lambs and the rams of Bashan and goats, and Ezekiel says God will judge between the rams and the he-goats, between the fat cattle and the lean.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the he-goat's story is about leadership, because the strong push the weak aside and God notices. The dream that made Jacob rich and the judgment that separates the rams are the same word, and I hold that the Chief Shepherd will sort His flock Himself.
